rows.basis: Revenue of the Cloud Memory Business Unit (hyperscale cloud memory and all HBM), the AI line. Excluded: CDBU $37.592bn (data center, but it includes enterprise storage and non-AI DRAM), MCBU and AEBU. The 10-K's ~60% data-center share is a market share, not an AI share. The $5.687bn CDBU statement is a single quarter.

CMBU revenue, up 257% on 'accelerating AI demand in cloud server markets for HBM' (MD&A). CDBU $7.229bn is excluded. The '>50% data center' statement is one quarter's data-center mix, not an AI share.
CMBU revenue as recast to the fiscal-2025 segment structure. The fact has no XBRL reference. The reported FY2024 segment was CNBU ($9.513bn, which includes client and graphics), and it is not used.
CMBU revenue as recast to the fiscal-2025 segment structure. The fact has no XBRL reference. The reported FY2023 CNBU ($5.71bn) included client and graphics and is not used.

Compute and Networking BU revenue, the only data-center-bearing segment before the 2025 recast. It includes client PC and graphics DRAM, so it overstates AI exposure heavily and is not comparable to CMBU.

Micron says it is 'investing in our global manufacturing footprint to support [customers'] growing demand' in 'the AI era'. That is the whole capex ($30.712bn gross), with no HBM or AI share stated, so no amount is attributed.
The May 2025 release ties 'disciplined investments' to 'growing AI-driven memory demand'. That is the total capex ($15.857bn), with no AI or HBM split stated.
The outlook statement says investments will 'satisfy growing AI-driven memory demand'. It gives no amount and no AI share.
